 * @id py/code-injection
 * @tags security

import python
import semmle.python.dataflow.new.DataFlow
import semmle.python.dataflow.new.TaintTracking
import semmle.python.dataflow.new.RemoteFlowSources
import semmle.python.Concepts

module CodeInjectionConfig implements DataFlow::ConfigSig {
  predicate isSource(DataFlow::Node source) {
    source instanceof RemoteFlowSource
  }

  predicate isSink(DataFlow::Node sink) {
    sink = any(CodeExecution ce).getCode()
  }
}

module CodeInjectionFlow = TaintTracking::Global<CodeInjectionConfig>;
import CodeInjectionFlow::PathGraph

from CodeInjectionFlow::PathNode source, CodeInjectionFlow::PathNode sink
where CodeInjectionFlow::flowPath(source, sink)
select sink.getNode(), source, sink, "Code injection from $@.", source.getNode(), "user input"
findings.hypothesis: Code injection via eval/exec with untrusted HTTP input

/**
 * @name Unsafe response header parsing
 * @description Potential HTTP response splitting via response headers
 * @kind path-problem
 * @problem.severity error
 * @id py/http-response-splitting
 * @tags security
 *        external/cwe/cwe-113
 */

import python
import semmle.python.dataflow.new.DataFlow
import semmle.python.dataflow.new.TaintTracking
import semmle.python.dataflow.new.RemoteFlowSources
import semmle.python.Concepts
import semmle.python.ApiGraphs

module ResponseSplittingConfig implements DataFlow::ConfigSig {
  predicate isSource(DataFlow::Node source) {
    source instanceof RemoteFlowSource
  }

  predicate isSink(DataFlow::Node sink) {
    exists(API::CallNode call |
      call = API::moduleImport("aiohttp").getMember("web").getMember("Response").getMember("headers").getMember(["add", "__setitem__"]).getACall() and
      sink = call.getArg(1)
    )
  }
}

module ResponseSplittingFlow = TaintTracking::Global<ResponseSplittingConfig>;
import ResponseSplittingFlow::PathGraph

from ResponseSplittingFlow::PathNode source, ResponseSplittingFlow::PathNode sink
where ResponseSplittingFlow::flowPath(source, sink)
select sink.getNode(), source, sink, "HTTP response splitting via headers from $@.", source.getNode(), "user input"
findings.hypothesis: HTTP response splitting via untrusted data in response headers

/**
 * @name Path traversal vulnerability
 * @description User-controlled input used in file system operations leading to path traversal
 * @kind path-problem
 * @problem.severity error
 * @id py/path-traversal
 * @tags security
 *        external/cwe/cwe-022
 */

import python
import semmle.python.dataflow.new.DataFlow
import semmle.python.dataflow.new.TaintTracking
import semmle.python.dataflow.new.RemoteFlowSources
import semmle.python.Concepts
import semmle.python.ApiGraphs

module PathTraversalConfig implements DataFlow::ConfigSig {
  predicate isSource(DataFlow::Node source) {
    source instanceof RemoteFlowSource
  }

  predicate isSink(DataFlow::Node sink) {
    exists(API::CallNode call |
      call = API::moduleImport("os").getMember(["path", "join"]).getACall() and
      sink = call.getArg(0)
    ) or
    exists(API::CallNode call |
      call = API::moduleImport("pathlib").getMember("Path").getACall() and
      sink = call.getArg(0)
    ) or
    exists(API::CallNode call |
      call = API::moduleImport("builtins").getMember("open").getACall() and
      sink = call.getArg(0)
    )
  }
}

module PathTraversalFlow = TaintTracking::Global<PathTraversalConfig>;
import PathTraversalFlow::PathGraph

from PathTraversalFlow::PathNode source, PathTraversalFlow::PathNode sink
where PathTraversalFlow::flowPath(source, sink)
select sink.getNode(), source, sink, "Path traversal from $@.", source.getNode(), "user input"
findings.hypothesis: Path traversal vulnerability in file operations with user-controlled input
Path traversal vulnerabilities in multipart file upload handling could allow attackers to read/write arbitrary files

/**
 * @name XML External Entity (XXE) processing
 * @description Using XML parsers with external entity processing enabled
 * @kind problem
 * @problem.severity error
 * @id py/xxe-aiohttp
 * @tags security
 *        external/cwe/cwe-611
 */

import python
import semmle.python.ApiGraphs

from DataFlow::CallCfgNode call
where
  // Look for XML parsing in aiohttp context
  call = API::moduleImport("xml").getMember(["etree", "ElementTree"]).getMember(["parse", "fromstring"]).getACall() or
  call = API::moduleImport("lxml").getMember(["etree"]).getMember(["parse", "fromstring", "XMLParser"]).getACall()
select call, "Potentially unsafe XML parsing that could lead to XXE attacks if user input is processed without disabling external entities."
findings.hypothesis: XML external entity (XXE) vulnerabilities in XML parsing
